s1: City of Elmina. Seven forty-two in the evening. Uncle Lim takes his usual walk through the mall lobby... [[slnc 500]] and collapses. [[slnc 900]] The lobby camera sees it all. But nobody is watching. [[slnc 1200]] Four seconds later, TanyaCCTV raises an alert. Someone has stopped moving, and may need help. [[slnc 400]] Officer Hafiz is already on his way.
s2: In two thousand and nine, Sime Darby Property helped pioneer the Safe City Initiative in Ara Damansara. Twenty-two cameras, linked to the police. [[slnc 500]] Today, a township spans thousands of acres, with hundreds of cameras, recording more footage than any team could ever watch. So most of it is only seen after something has gone wrong. [[slnc 600]] We built TanyaCCTV to change that. To turn a township's cameras, from recorders, into responders.
s3: Bandar Bukit Raja. Three thirty in the morning. [[slnc 400]] This is TanyaCCTV's Live Monitor. The guard drew one zone, and marked one motorbike to protect. That is all the setup it needs. [[slnc 600]] Movement in the parking bay. [[slnc 500]] Then, a warning. Someone is at the motorbike, almost forty seconds before it is taken. Enough time to send a patrol. [[slnc 700]] And the moment the motorbike moves, the alarm. [[slnc 900]] One click opens the clip, and TanyaCCTV follows the suspect, frame by frame.
s4: The next morning, another resident reports a stolen motorbike. [[slnc 300]] No more scrubbing through hours of footage. Officer Hafiz simply describes what he is looking for. [[slnc 1500]] In seconds, the garage, at three minutes past four. A man, loading a motorbike onto a truck. [[slnc 600]] When he walks out of view, TanyaCCTV knows, and picks him up again the moment he returns. [[slnc 400]] Hours of footage, reduced to the moments that matter.
s5: Every camera in the township lives on one map, so the team sees where things happen, not just what. [[slnc 500]] When someone needs to be found, TanyaCCTV follows them from camera to camera, and draws their route. [[slnc 700]] And it watches over belongings too. At the transit hub, a bag left alone is flagged, before anyone reports it missing.
s6: Every moment can become evidence. Clips are gathered into an investigation, and laid out on one timeline, across cameras. Every clip is fingerprinted, so the report handed to the auxiliary police can be trusted. [[slnc 500]] And a person confirms every alert. TanyaCCTV says what it sees. Never who someone is, or what they intend.
s7: Back at the mall, Uncle Lim is sitting up, talking to the paramedics. [[slnc 400]] He was reached in minutes, because this time, someone was watching. [[slnc 800]] TanyaCCTV works with the cameras a township already has, runs on a single computer, and keeps every recording on site. [[slnc 500]] It finds any moment in seconds, and warns you before it happens. [[slnc 900]] TanyaCCTV. Your township's cameras, now listening.
